A key distinction between definite and indefinite integrals is that (assuming other parameters are specified)
the definite integral has a specific numerical value, while the indefinite integral is a function

If you remember that the integral means the area under the curve, then this distinction makes sense and is easy to remember – the area under a curve does not have a specific value until you specify starting and ending values.

In many applications it is useful to approximate the values of a function in the neighborhood of a point as polynomials using the derivatives at that point.
